title: +*POWER AND JUSTICE IN U.S. NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT
description: Explores the role of systems of oppression in natural resource management in the U.S. from history to present.  Emphasizes the roles of policies and social norms in creating structural inequities to land use, environmental governance, and engaging in the scientific process.
registration_restrictions:
Students with a term class standing of Freshman or Sophomore may not enroll.

Enrollment is limited to students with a program in:

  • Fish, Wildlife & Conserv Scien (018)
  • Bioresource Research (113)
  • Crop and Soil Science (120)
  • Horticulture (145)
  • Environmental Econ and Policy (237)
  • Agricultural Sciences (259)
  • Rangeland Sciences (292)
  • Ecological Engineering (450)
  • Biology (509)
  • Botany (515)
  • Zoology (620)
  • Environmental Sciences (657)
  • Natural Resources (671)
  • Fisheries & Wildlife Sciences (733)
  • Biological Data Sciences (858)
  • Sustainability (870)
  • Tourism, Rec, & Adventure Lead (872)
  • Agricultural & Food Bus Mgmt (897)
recommendations: Completion of a Difference, Power, and Oppression Foundations course
